key_insight: A surrogate-assisted inverse-design workflow can rapidly find an all-oxide TPV emitter geometry that achieves high, narrowband emission near a target wavelength.
engineering_relevance: This offers a high-temperature-stable alternative to metal-based emitters for thermophotovoltaic systems, improving spectral matching to the cell bandgap while reducing thermal degradation risk.
method: Trained ExtraTrees surrogate models on FDTD-generated spectra from systematic sweeps of ITO, Al2O3, and period parameters.
Used Bayesian optimization on a penalty-augmented objective to enforce E_peak > 0.90 while minimizing FWHM and maximizing in-band fraction.
Validated the optimized design with full FDTD simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports optimization and validation against FDTD data using emission metrics including peak emission, peak wavelength, FWHM, and in-band fraction.
watch_item: The optimized design depends on the surrogate’s coverage of the sampled design space, so performance may drop if fabrication tolerances or material properties deviate from the training assumptions.
paper_title: Surrogate-Assisted Inverse Design and Temperature-Dependent Electrothermal Analysis of an All-Oxide Narrowband Thermophotovoltaic Emitter
